name: Leaders of the Fang
summary: In the Wailing Caverns, four leaders of the Druids of the Fang threaten the Barrens. Nara Wildmane sends Horde champions from Thunder Bluff to slay them and take their twisted dream gems. If the druids are not stopped, their serpentine nightmare may claim the land.

sections.title: A Vision Corrupted
sections.body: Naralex, a night elf druid, entered the Wailing Caverns' underground springs. He hoped the Emerald Dream would bring life back to the dry Barrens. But when he fell asleep, his dream became a nightmare. The acolytes who came with him abandoned nature's harmony and fell under its corruption. They became the Druids of the Fang.

sections.title: The Four Dream Gems
sections.body: Four leaders of the Druids of the Fang carry dream gems that channel warped dream energy. They hope to reshape the Barrens into their own viperous Eden. Lord Cobrahn, Lady Anacondra, Lord Pythas, and Lord Serpentis each carry one gem. While the gems remain with them, corruption spreads through Kalimdor's soil and waters.

sections.title: A Burden Lifted in Thunder Bluff
sections.body: From Thunder Bluff, Nara Wildmane watches over nature's balance, yet the caverns' torment reaches her mind. The four serpent lords and their gems hold the sect together. Taking the gems breaks their command and frees Nara from lingering nightmares. It also protects the surrounding plains from unnatural blight.

faq.q: Who are the leaders of the Druids of the Fang?
aliases: who leads druids of the fang
faq.answer: The Druids of the Fang are led by four fallen druids: Lady Anacondra, Lord Cobrahn, Lord Pythas, and Lord Serpentis. They abandoned their original nature teachings, took serpent forms, and wield nightmare magic in the Wailing Caverns.
Each of the four leaders in the Wailing Caverns carries a dream gem. The gems focus the nightmare-tainted energy from Naralex's slumber and fuel the sect's efforts to change the Barrens.

faq.q: Why does Nara Wildmane want the gems?
faq.answer: Nara Wildmane is a tauren druid in Thunder Bluff who feels the nightmare's spiritual ripples. The corrupted leaders haunt her dreams, and she wants their power broken to protect her mind and the Barrens.

faq.q: Were the Druids of the Fang always evil?
aliases: why did the druids turn bad
faq.answer: No. The Druids of the Fang were once noble night elf druids who followed Naralex into the caverns to heal the dry savanna. When Naralex fell into a nightmare, its energies warped their minds and made them a fanatical snake cult.

faq.q: Where is this quest turned in?
aliases: leaders of the fang turn in
hand in leaders of the fang
faq.answer: You bring all four gems to Nara Wildmane on the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. After gathering them in the Wailing Caverns, you travel back to Mulgore to deliver them.

faq.q: Does killing the leaders cure Naralex?
faq.answer: Slaying the four leaders breaks the sect's upper ranks and halts the spread of their ritual, but Naralex does not wake from this alone. Other druidic rites deeper in the caverns are needed to awaken him.

angles.text: As a tauren druid, you may feel the Druids of the Fang's corruption deeply. They twist the Emerald Dream into poisonous blight, an affront to Cenarion principles.
As a member of the Horde, you know the Barrens connects Orgrimmar, Thunder Bluff, and the Darkspear isles. Serpent worshipers changing the land threaten the stability of the whole Horde.
As a tauren, you hold the Earth Mother's health at the heart of your faith. Corruption spreading from the Barrens' springs profanes the land you roam.
